fichas.title: Steel column with conventional plaster surround
fichas.summary: A steel column is enclosed by a conventional plaster surround with an edge protector, wired fabric, binding wire, ribbed expanded metal, and a masonry or cemented core. The figure identifies the assembly as F 90.
uses: Fire protection of a steel column

dimensions.label: Ground lime or lime-cement plaster thickness
dimensions.context: Plaster surround; OCR specifies mortar group I or II according to DIN 18550.
dimensions.ocr_raw: 2.5 mm ground lime or lime cement plaster, of mortar group I or II acc. DIN 18550

dimensions.label: Spacer thickness
dimensions.context: Expanded metal and round steel used as spacer; OCR indicates a minimum.

dimensions.label: Core height above floor
dimensions.context: Minimum height; core to be brick/masonry lined or cemented.
dimensions.ocr_raw: Core, min. 1.5 m above the floor, brick/masonry lined or cemented

fichas.title: Steel column with fire-protection boards
fichas.summary: A steel column is enclosed in fire-protection boards with staggered joints, fixed with wire clamps or drywall screws. The cladding thickness depends on the profile dimensions and required fire-resistance class; the figure labels profile height, profile width, and cladding thickness.
uses: Fire protection of a steel column

dimensions.label: Dimension shown on detail
dimensions.context: A numeric dimension is printed beside the illustrated board-clad column; the OCR does not identify its measurement axis or unit.

fichas.title: Fire-protection cladding for steel support beams
fichas.summary: A steel support beam is clad with fire-protection boards. The detail identifies fixing pieces, an extra piece behind the joint, and profile height and width. The figure gives fire-resistance classes F 30 A–F 180 A.
uses: Fire protection of a steel support beam

fichas.title: Lightweight fibre-silicate partition
fichas.summary: Principle detail of a lightweight fibre-silicate partition, including a wall connection and butt-joint detail. The figure identifies the assembly as F 30 A.
uses: Separating spaces with a fire-resisting partition

dimensions.label: Dimension shown in wall-connection detail
dimensions.context: Numeric dimension printed at the connection detail; OCR gives “100” but does not identify the dimension axis or unit.

fichas.title: Timber stud wall
fichas.summary: Principle detail of a timber stud wall with a wall-connection detail. The figure identifies the assembly as F 30 B.
uses: Separating spaces with a fire-resisting wall

dimensions.label: Dimension shown in wall detail
dimensions.context: Numeric dimension printed across the wall detail; OCR gives “625” but does not identify the dimension axis or unit.

fichas.title: External wall component with thermal insulation
fichas.summary: Principle detail of an external wall component with thermal insulation and a wall connection. The figure identifies the assembly as W 90.
uses: External wall fire protection and insulation

fichas.title: Stable fibre-silicate partition with C-profile studs
fichas.summary: Principle detail of a fibre-silicate partition using C-profile studs, shown with a wall connection and butt-joint detail. The figure identifies the assembly as F 90 A.

fichas.title: Fire-protection requirements for walls and columns
fichas.summary: Text outlines MBO fire-protection requirements for load-bearing, bracing, and external walls and columns by building class. It also discusses separating-wall continuity and openings, fire-protection claddings for steel columns and beams, and construction options for non-load-bearing partitions. A table selects construction materials and their fire classes, certificates, and marks.
uses: Establishing fire-resistance requirements for building components
Selecting construction materials and fire-protection assemblies
